name: The Historic Inner City
tagline: The UNESCO quarter of white wooden Dutch buildings
description: The colonial core around the Waterkant and Onafhankelijkheidsplein, a UNESCO World Heritage site of white-painted wooden Dutch buildings, with Fort Zeelandia at one end and the enormous wooden cathedral behind. It is flat, compact and entirely walkable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to be inside the World Heritage area
pros: The finest wooden colonial architecture in the Americas

name: Centrum and the Keizerstraat
tagline: Where the mosque and the synagogue share a car park
description: The commercial streets just inland from the historic front, holding the Central Market, the shops and the Keizerstraat, where the Neveh Shalom synagogue and the Ahmadiyya mosque stand side by side and share their parking. It is the image the country uses of itself.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the markets and the everyday city
pros: The Central Market and the food stalls
The mosque and synagogue on the same street

name: Zorg en Hoop and Uitvlugt
tagline: The residential suburbs southwest of the centre
description: Quieter residential districts a few kilometres from the historic core, with the small Zorg en Hoop airfield that serves the interior, supermarkets and the housing most of Paramaribo's professional population uses. Rents are lower and the streets are wider.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space and everyday services
pros: Zorg en Hoop airfield for interior flights
cons: A car or regular taxis are needed

name: Blauwgrond
tagline: The Javanese quarter and its warungs
description: A district northeast of the centre settled by Javanese Surinamese, whose warungs serve Indonesian food from open kitchens at prices that are almost nothing. It is where Paramaribo eats in the evening and one of the clearest expressions of the country's mix.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is the food
pros: The best and cheapest eating in Suriname
